name: Ghisulal Rathod
current_role: Founder, Cello group; former non-executive chairman of Wim Plast Ltd (1988-2020)
profile: Ghisulal Dhanraj Rathod founded the Mumbai-based Cello plastics group, starting with plastic bangles and PVC footwear in Goregaon before building the Cello brand of housewares, writing instruments and furniture; Wim Plast (Cello moulded furniture) was a listed group company. The business is now run by his sons Pradeep and Pankaj and grandson Gaurav via Cello World Ltd (listed 2023).
interesting_fact: Cello started in 1967 with seven machines and about sixty workers making plastic bangles and PVC footwear in Goregaon, Mumbai, and grew into one of India's best-known consumerware brands.
deep_cut_fact: After seeing American households store food in round plastic containers on a US trip, he launched insulated casseroles in India in the late 1980s, a product that became a Cello staple.
notes: Patriarch, likely elderly and not public-facing; sources differ on founding dates (1962/1967/1974). Day-to-day leadership is son Pradeep Rathod (CMD, Cello World), the more practical outreach target. Reports say Wim Plast was being merged into Cello Consumer Products (2026, unverified).

name: Sonal Yatin Kakodkar
current_role: Listed shareholder/family member associated with Parle Products (per Hurun India 2018-2019); no public executive role found
profile: Appears on Hurun India 2018-2019 (about US$132m) with wealth attributed to Parle Products, the Mumbai biscuit maker (Parle-G) founded in 1929 and controlled by the Chauhan family. No public biography, interviews or executive role were found; she appears to be a passive family shareholder.
interesting_fact: Parle Products, the source of her listed wealth, became India's first packaged-food company to pass US$2bn in annual revenue (FY22).
notes: Very private; family relationship to the Parle Products Chauhans not publicly documented. Not a public-facing figure; only route is via Parle Products corporate.
